title: Innovation assessment
scope: LabourLens is a research prototype for Singapore labour-market analysts. It uses public statistics and MOM reports from Q1 2020 to Q2 2026, plus an MTI employment article.
abstract: I built LabourLens for analysts researching Singapore's labour market. It searches reports, looks up statistics, calculates changes in code and returns cited answers, asks for clarification or abstains when evidence is missing. I tested retrieval, answer checks, the bounded agent, MCP, security controls and operating costs. Retrieval improved on development questions, but full answer tests did not show a reliable gain on either test set. The prototype is not approved for government production use.
approach: Collected official statistics and reports. Each statistical row records its measure, unit, period, population, release and source. Reports become searchable passages; uncertain tables are flagged rather than guessed.

Compared exact-word keyword search with meaning search based on text embeddings, then combined their results. Period and release filters remove mismatched evidence; a second ranking pass orders what remains.

Built one bounded agent, historically evaluated with three read-only tools. The current served set has four: report search, statistics lookup, change calculation and rates-only annual_average. The last is a simple mean of four non-null quarterly rates from one series, not an official annual rate; it has not been re-evaluated.

Answers have a fixed structure, citations and short quotations. Code checks citation labels, quotations, reported numbers and answer status. These checks cannot prove that a quotation supports a claim.

The current served prompts are planner_v7, answer_v9, triage_v4 and contextualise_v3. Resolved questions and bounded series/period context support follow-ups as untrusted data. Reasons questions seek attributed MOM commentary, not inferred causation; abstention distinguishes missing observations from missing method or commentary. These changes are unevaluated.

Tested retrieval, a fixed workflow against the agent, model candidates, report-table calculation, direct and MCP routes, and synthetic attacks. Separate development, original and fresh question sets show what improved and what did not.

sections.title: How I would improve it
sections.summary: Each proposal says what I would change, why, and the check required before adoption. None is built or shown to work.
paragraphs: The live agent sends statistics lookup and annual averaging through MCP. The default server has ten read-only tools, two used by the agent. The historical three-tool all-MCP variant was slower with no demonstrated quality gain in a one-run, 65-question sample and was not adopted; removing statistics also removed calculator inputs. Neither measurement evaluates annual averaging or the current prompts.

Evaluated median answer time was about 14 seconds, with chained model calls. A served native-tool, reasoning-off smoke took 29.8, 7.8 and 9.1 seconds versus 53.1, 8.6 and 12.8 for structured planning: three questions, once each, accuracy unmeasured. Streaming is shipped to show progress, not to shorten full-answer time.

Neither Decisions API trial was adopted. In v1, the primary router matched 397/409 routes per repeat, diverted one legitimate question and recalled only 19/30 non-in-scope cases; the verifier falsely supported 44/58 partially supported claims. Dev-tuned v2 matched 414/450 repeat rows, diverted two distinct in-scope questions and returned provider refusals on all 30 serious-harm presentations. Its case-median p50/p95 was 0.362/0.426 seconds versus chat's 1.392/1.847, but speed did not repair failed safety, quality and operational gates. These are AI-labelled screens, not human accuracy or an end-to-end speedup.

subsections.title: Retrieval and answer quality
paragraphs: I compared BM25 keyword search, embedding-based meaning search and a hybrid on the same development questions. Filtering by period and release, then reranking the candidates, raised the share of relevant passages in the first eight results from 54% to 97%. This measures passage retrieval, not answer accuracy.

Filtering and reranking also found the known passage more often on small original and fresh test subsets. Full-system comparisons did not show a reliable answer gain on either set. Development shaped the design, the original test shares evidence with it, and fresh questions have since been reused. Treat these as diagnostics, not proof of general improvement.

I also tested arithmetic on figures extracted from report text. The extension failed pre-set development checks and was not adopted. The current calculator uses validated statistical rows; report tables still need reliable cell, unit and row-to-column extraction before they can be calculation inputs.

subsections.title: Drift detection
paragraphs: The data pipeline stores versioned snapshots and provenance. An operator still has to acquire and rebuild the data; scheduled refresh, automatic drift alerts and rollback have not been implemented. The expanded source corpus and newer served planner were not re-evaluated, so the older scores do not describe those changes.

proposals.title: Reduce waiting without lowering answer quality
proposals.gap: The evaluated median is about 14 seconds because model calls are chained, and streaming only shows progress.
proposals.measure: Run triage in parallel with the first retrieval and planning step, cache embeddings and repeated series lookups, test prompt and permission-scoped response caching, skip contextualisation without history, try a smaller triage model, and run independent read-only tools in parallel, up to three calls per round within the existing total budget. Key caches by permissions, corpus, prompts and model.
proposals.threshold: Compare paired p50 and p95 full-answer latency, accuracy, safety and cost with the served baseline on the same 237 development questions, then on fresh blind cases. Adopt nothing that lowers accuracy or weakens citation, numerical, abstention or safety checks.

proposals.title: Third Decisions attempt: preregistered two-way scope gate
proposals.gap: Both Decisions trials were faster but failed safety, quality and operations, and a two-way scope gate is untested.
proposals.measure: Untested, with no paid execution authorised: after existing harm and small-talk handling, a frozen in-scope or out-of-scope Decisions gate with agent fallback runs against chat on 150 fresh human-labelled cases (90 in-scope, 30 out-of-scope, 15 harm, 15 small-talk), three interleaved repeats, confidence 0.70 and no tuning.
proposals.threshold: Each repeat needs zero legitimate diversions, 148/150 correct routes, 29/30 out-of-scope recalls, at most 1% failures over 450 scheduled classifications per arm, p50 and p95 within 80% of chat, and no downstream safety regression. Owner approval comes before execution or adoption.

proposals.title: Evaluate annual averaging and new tools
proposals.gap: annual_average and the new prompts are unevaluated, and its simple mean is not an official annual rate.
proposals.measure: Evaluate all four served tools end to end, including four-quarter completeness, nulls and series consistency, and add other typed read-only tools only for a demonstrated evidence gap.
proposals.threshold: Pass deterministic boundary cases, then compare accuracy, false answers, citations, latency and cost with the three-tool baseline.

proposals.title: Report-table arithmetic
proposals.gap: Flattened report tables can attach a value to the wrong row or column, and the earlier extension failed.
proposals.measure: Pre-register one extraction change that checks cell, row, column, unit and population lineage, excludes uncertain cells and tests known cases before new blind questions.
proposals.threshold: Reach at least 0.50 accuracy on predefined numerical cases without a higher false-answer rate or weaker definition and citation checks.

proposals.title: Blind re-review and per-layer ablations
proposals.gap: One reviewer, AI-drafted labels and bundled changes cannot show true accuracy or which layer helps.
proposals.measure: Have three analysts label a stratified blind set before seeing AI suggestions, then adjudicate, and test each retrieval filter, reranker, prompt guard and output check separately with harmless look-alikes.
proposals.threshold: Target Fleiss kappa of at least 0.70 and an accuracy interval no wider than 0.10, report misses and false alarms per layer, and never tune on the blind set.

proposals.title: Gold cases for 2020 to 2023
proposals.gap: The served window reaches 2020, but every evaluated question covers 2024 to 2026.
proposals.measure: Write fresh 2020 to 2023 questions with expected evidence, definitions, revisions and abstention labels, independently reviewed before any run.
proposals.threshold: Report retrieval and answer quality by year and question family with uncertainty, and keep blind cases out of tuning.

proposals.title: Scheduled refresh and source onboarding
proposals.gap: Published datasets change, and a rebuild still needs an operator.
proposals.measure: Fetch approved sources on a schedule into immutable snapshots, validate schema, coverage, revisions and licence before promotion, and mark old data stale.
proposals.threshold: Reject failed snapshots, alert on missed freshness targets and evaluate each new source before serving it.

proposals.title: Add coverage carefully
proposals.gap: Some series, periods, source versions and languages are not represented.
proposals.measure: Add reviewed MOM, SingStat and other government sources through the same manifest, rights review and evaluation process.
proposals.threshold: Keep revision-conflict, definition and citation performance at the approved baseline before serving a new source.

sections.title: Production deployment and security
sections.summary: A proposed production design. Nothing here is deployed, or shown to meet a standard.
paragraphs: Built today: one DigitalOcean Droplet behind Caddy with Docker Compose and GitHub Actions, an access-code gate, rights-scan checks, a synthetic threat suite and audit IDs. It uses one application worker; budget and audit state are local files and request limits are in memory. Government identity, provider-side spend caps, load behaviour and rollback are not verified.

subsections.title: Provenance, explainability and review
paragraphs: The workbench shows source links, cited passages, answer status and tool activity. Feedback is stored with the run, but it does not yet change the system. A citation validator confirms that labels and quotations came from supplied evidence; it cannot determine whether the evidence entails the claim.

subsections.title: Security, privacy and third-party risk
paragraphs: The agent has typed, read-only tools, bounded calls and validated MCP replies. Retrieved passages are evidence, not instructions. In one three-repeat synthetic attack comparison, the guarded configuration passed 50 of 54 attack cases, compared with 42 of 54 for the naive configuration. The answer prompt and guards changed together, so this does not identify which defence helped. Both configurations also failed three of eight harmless look-alike cases. These tests do not establish resistance to adaptive attacks or a specific defence layer's effect.

subsections.title: Mocked or unverified components and their production replacements
paragraphs: No live capability is mocked; hostile-server cases are synthetic tests. The table lists what is unverified today and the proposed replacement.

proposals.title: Production architecture, not deployed
proposals.gap: The single-worker prototype keeps budget and audit state locally and cannot show shared-state reliability.
proposals.measure: Put edge/WAF and SSO in front of a load balancer and stateless API replicas, with a bounded queue, research workers and an SSE event store, separate ingestion into immutable object storage, read-only versioned search and DuckDB snapshots, an isolated MCP service, shared budgets, rate limits and audit state, a secrets manager, an approved LLM gateway, observability, CI gates, rollback and encrypted backups with restore drills.
proposals.threshold: Demonstrate load, queue exhaustion, reconnect, timeout, rollback and restore behaviour before replicas serve users.

proposals.title: Identity, roles and data classification
proposals.gap: Shared access codes cannot separate users or restricted sources.
proposals.measure: Use SSO with per-user RBAC, and label departments, sources and passages with classifications enforced before retrieval, caching and tool use.
proposals.threshold: Show cross-user denial and no restricted text in prompts, caches or logs.

proposals.title: Secrets, WAF and rate limits
proposals.gap: Local files and in-memory limits do not survive replicas or restarts.
proposals.measure: Keep secrets in a managed store with rotation, put a WAF and shared per-user rate limits at the edge, and cap provider spend at the gateway.
proposals.threshold: Test rotation, rate-limit and budget exhaustion across replicas.

proposals.title: Audit retention and tamper evidence
proposals.gap: Local audit files can be edited or lost.
proposals.measure: Keep structured, tamper-evident audit records with hash chaining or write-once storage, defined retention and restricted reader access.
proposals.threshold: Verify that edits and deletions are detected and retention is enforced.

proposals.title: Injection and egress controls
proposals.gap: The synthetic attack tests do not cover adaptive attacks.
proposals.measure: Keep retrieved text as untrusted data, isolate MCP, allow-list outbound hosts and block other egress from tools and models.
proposals.threshold: Run independent paraphrases, hostile passages and unsafe tool requests with harmless look-alikes, and record blocked egress.

proposals.title: Supply chain and penetration testing
proposals.gap: The prototype has no independent security assessment.
proposals.measure: Pin and scan dependencies and images, keep an inventory, and commission independent penetration testing before restricted data is admitted.
proposals.threshold: Close critical findings and rerun the tests after fixes.

proposals.title: Provider data use and PDPA review
proposals.gap: The external model route has unverified residency and provider terms.
proposals.measure: Have authorised legal and privacy teams review residency, provider data use, retention and PDPA obligations before choosing model endpoints.
proposals.threshold: Record the decision and approved endpoints, and block unapproved endpoints at the gateway.

proposals.title: Feedback review loop
proposals.gap: Votes and comments are stored but do not produce regression tests.
proposals.measure: Review every thumbs-down and a sample of thumbs-up, write one test with expected evidence for each confirmed failure, and change one thing at a time. Pseudonymise comments and limit retention.
proposals.threshold: Every confirmed failure has a reviewed case and a recorded change; never train on unreviewed votes.

proposals.title: Resilience, SLOs and cost caps
proposals.gap: One Droplet and one worker have no verified recovery.
proposals.measure: Set SLOs from a measured workload, assign on-call ownership, enforce cost caps, and test backups, disaster recovery and failover.
proposals.threshold: Approve recovery objectives and show restore, failover and budget-exhaustion drills.

proposals.title: Staged technical path
proposals.gap: A broad launch would extend unverified assumptions.
proposals.measure: Move from a public-data pilot to a hardened beta only after identity, security, evaluation and recovery gates pass.
proposals.threshold: Record acceptance evidence, stop criteria and rollback at each stage; no time promise is implied.

sections.title: Making it ready for government use across departments
sections.summary: A proposed operating model for several departments. It is not a deployment or a compliance claim.
paragraphs: Departmental security, legal, data-owner and operational approval remain necessary. Nothing here establishes compliance with any framework.

proposals.title: Governance and human accountability
proposals.gap: Outputs are fallible and the current evaluation is not independent ground truth.
proposals.measure: Use the Singapore Model AI Governance Framework as a review reference, with a risk and impact assessment, accountable owners, human-in-the-loop review of consequential decisions, model and system cards, change control, CI evaluation gates and drift monitoring.
proposals.threshold: Department owners approve controls and acceptance criteria; any framework alignment or compliance claim needs an authorised assessment.

proposals.title: Multi-department use
proposals.gap: A shared service could leak evidence or mix departmental definitions.
proposals.measure: Isolate tenants, department corpora, roles and caches, share MCP only through authenticated read-only contracts, and require ingestion specifications and a licence register for every source.
proposals.threshold: Test cross-tenant isolation in search, tools, caches and logs, and verify licences before onboarding.

proposals.title: Department rollout
proposals.gap: Each department adds its own data, definitions and risks.
proposals.measure: Roll out department by department after data-owner approval, isolation tests, training and support readiness.
proposals.threshold: Record sign-off and stop criteria for each department; no timeline, readiness or compliance claim is implied.

limitations: Development questions shaped the design. The original test shares evidence with development; fresh questions have since been reused. Neither test demonstrated an answer-quality gain.

Questions and reference labels were AI-drafted and signed off by one human reviewer. The primary answer judge belongs to the same provider family as the generator. This is not independent ground truth.
Citation checks confirm the mechanics of a quote, not that it supports a claim. Arithmetic can still use the wrong inputs. Synthetic attacks do not establish general security.

Final comparisons used an earlier corpus and planner than the expanded live system. The newer corpus and served planner have not been re-evaluated. Monitoring, rollback, government identity, provider limits and production scale remain unverified.

components.current: Shared demo codes; Caddy and one application worker.
components.replacement: Proposed: edge/WAF, SSO, load balancer and stateless API replicas; source roles checked before retrieval.

components.current: Request-scoped agent and streamed progress; no durable queue.
components.replacement: Proposed: bounded queue, research workers and SSE event store; shared budget, rate-limit and audit state.

components.current: Local snapshots, search indexes, DuckDB and read-only MCP.
components.replacement: Proposed: separate ingestion; immutable object storage; versioned read-only search and DuckDB snapshots; isolated MCP service.

components.current: External model route; residency and provider terms unverified.
components.replacement: Proposed: secrets manager and approved LLM gateway enforcing endpoints, spend, retention and audit controls.

components.current: GitHub Actions deployment; production load, rollback and restore unverified.
components.replacement: Proposed: observability, CI quality/security/rights gates, atomic promotion, rollback, encrypted backups and restore drills.
